title: A new axiomatics, with a bounded objective
body: “Je voudrais définir une autre axiomatique” announces a replacement presentation of networks on a set of lieux: moderate pairs are primitive, and finite moderation is defined pairwise. This adds a concrete cut-based test case to the Esquisse’s program of reconstructing stratified objects from pieces, but the present page does not define a general form or give a reconstruction equivalence. S14 is therefore motivated here, not established.
context: E 119/27,32–34: pièces de construction; axiomatique; provisional systems. S §1.1 restates the current proposal.
check: carried as background without fault found

title: The finite moderate sets form a flag complex
body: The condition “P₂(T)⊂S₀” makes the finite moderate subsets exactly the cliques of the graph with vertex set L and edge set S₀, so they form an abstract simplicial complex determined by its edges. This is a useful finite combinatorial organization of the input, but supplies neither the complement partitions nor the attachment maps needed for geometric reconstruction. In particular it should not be identified with the flag-indexed spaces of the Esquisse merely because both constructions use finite flags.
context: E 119/36–37,58–59: Drap(I), pair tubes, and additional composition data.
outcome: Every subset of a clique is a clique; the edge relation alone specifies the finite moderate-set complex. No realization theorem checked.
confidence: High for the combinatorial statement: it is an immediate consequence of the displayed pairwise definition; no novelty claim.

title: The complement-recovery question is answered in the margin, but not safely proved
kind: self-flagged: a step he himself marks as unverified
body: “Question : T est-il connu quand on … C_L(T) ?” is followed by “l’inverse est-il vrai ? Oui” and a short attempted proof, then repeated as an affirmative NB. The proof needs a point in T′ outside T to be compatible with every point of T, a condition not supplied merely by T and T′ each being moderate. Thus this is a question the manuscript locally answers, whose answer must still be tested rather than silently treated as an open question or a valid theorem.
context: S §1.1 explicitly notices the missing compatibility; E 119/28–29 contrasts primitive pieces with actual geometric complements.
outcome: Checked the logical use of membership in C(T); individual moderation of T and T′ does not imply their union is moderate.

title: A valid tronçon with two different singleton cuts having the same complement
body: Take L=Q×{0,1}, ordered by (q,i)<(r,j) exactly when q<r; its two points a=(q,0), b=(q,1) at one level are incomparable, yet C({a})=C({b}) is the set of all other levels. This model satisfies the prose local/global directedness and divisibility axioms of scan 009, and its finite-chain gap partitions satisfy Dec₁–Dec₂, while no finite moderate set is maximal. Consequently the current axioms do not make T↦C(T) injective, even within the ordered model; the margin’s universal affirmative answer needs an additional separation hypothesis.
context: S §1.1 raises but does not settle this issue; S §1.5 / SA21-R3-08 supplies the doubled-line model for a different question. E 119/34 emphasizes testing provisional axioms.
outcome: Explicit twin-singleton counterexample verified, including the applicable cut finiteness/refinement axioms; see research/math_checks.md. Refines the scan003 assertion.
confidence: High: both complements and all stated hypotheses have explicit descriptions; not claimed new in the literature.

title: “Connected components” are initially equivalence classes
body: The classes of R_T are named “comp. connexes de C(T)” before a topology on L has been chosen. Their topological interpretation is therefore extra content, not a consequence of having an equivalence relation, and later interval examples over Q show why the distinction matters. The corresponding register warnings about component-only data are analogies, not proofs about this manuscript.

title: Recovering boundary data and all cuts from two-point cuts
body: “Je prévois que les axiomes impliquent” separates two expectations: frontier data (c) should follow from the partitions (b), and all partitions should follow from the two-point partitions. Scans 011–016 later give a recovery argument in the ordered model, but do not supply the full intrinsic axioms for arbitrary network data. The Esquisse’s explicit warning that some triple composition maps are not determined by adjacent pair data marks a limit on extending this special reconstruction pattern to general stratified objects.

title: The displayed provisional axioms do not yet determine the frontier
body: Let L be infinite, let every pair be moderate, and give each C(T)=L\T one indiscrete equivalence class for every finite T. Both frontier assignments ∂C(T)=∅ and ∂C(T)=T satisfy ∂C(T)⊂T and Dec₂, and Dec₁ has one class; the finite/cofinite and maximal-finite premises on scan005 never arise. Hence the displayed axioms alone leave (c) underdetermined even when every R_T is fixed, identifying a missing requirement rather than refuting his prediction about a completed axiom system.
context: E 119/34: provisional axioms may require additions after concrete tests; S §2 leaves the general (c)-from-(b) task open.
outcome: Two distinct frontier structures on identical pair and partition data checked against exactly the currently displayed axioms; detailed hypothesis boundary in research/math_checks.md.
confidence: High under the explicitly stated axiom list; a stronger unwritten intended axiom could exclude the example.

title: The discrete example is not a universal finiteness conclusion
body: The page specifies a discrete network and proposes that a maximal finite moderate T must be all of L, with the resulting structure discrete. This rules out finite maximal cuts in a nondiscrete infinite model, but does not assert that L itself is finite or that every complete moderate-pair graph has the discrete partition structure. The distinction matters for the countermodel in SP31-N004-02 and for any proposed finite reconstruction of an infinite form.
context: E 119/32–34: local moderate models and provisional axioms; S §1.1 summarizes this discrete test.

This is closely parallel to the Esquisse’s admission that concrete tests may force extra or different axioms.

title: Dec₂ gives a coherent finite-set refinement system
body: For T⊂S, the unique containing component in Dec₂ defines a map from the finite class set of C(S) to that of C(T). For T⊂S⊂U, the direct map and the composite agree by the same uniqueness, so the written axiom already gives coherent transition maps on the inclusion category of moderate cuts. This is a genuine ingredient for S14, although neither cofilteredness of that category nor a geometric reconstruction theorem follows.
context: E 119/36–37: a system indexed by flags with additional maps and structure; packet README S14.
outcome: Transition-map composition follows from uniqueness of the containing R_T class, using nonempty equivalence classes; only this formal coherence checked.

Density and absence of endpoints make those order pieces nonempty, but on Q the corresponding ordinary order-topological intervals are not connected. Read this as the model’s prescribed cut partition unless an additional topological connectedness hypothesis is given; the frozen final interval’s closing bracket and absent plus sign remain diplomatic readings.

title: The obvious finite-chain index is not generally cofiltered
locus: finite chains as moderate cuts; compared with 010
body: If u and v are incomparable, their singleton cuts have no common upper bound in the poset of finite moderate subsets, because a finite chain cannot contain both. Thus reversing the inclusion refinement order does not automatically give the cofiltered index required for the naive pro-object version of S14. A larger category of cuttings or a compatibility restriction might address this obstruction; the broad planning guess is not refuted.
context: E 119/36–37; packet README S14; research/context_links.md CTX-OWN1.
outcome: The missing common refinement is a direct consequence of finite moderation being the chain condition; no claim about every possible pro-object presentation.
confidence: High for this specific index obstruction; alternative indexing constructions remain open.

title: Order reversal loses orientation but preserves the cut data
body: “Elle ne dépend que du biordre” asserts invariance when the order is replaced by its opposite. The same comparable pairs and the same unlabeled interval pieces survive, while their left/right ordering is reversed; this explains why the later reconstruction aims at an order up to reversal. It is a statement about these data on L, not an isotopy or homotopy equivalence of the spaces envisioned in the Esquisse.

locus: Partie modérée and final frontier sentence

This advances beyond finite moderate subsets of lieux, so the two uses of moderate should not be conflated. S reports that 156-7/071 later renames the classes, but that retrospective terminology is context only and was not imported into the transcription.

title: The order axioms do not force a linearly ordered or one-dimensional object
body: On R² define u≤ₛv to mean u=v or both coordinates of u are strictly smaller than those of v. This non-total order is directed both ways, divisible, and has directed nonempty strict cones, so it satisfies the prose tronçon conditions; its strict intervals are ordinary open rectangles. Thus those conditions alone admit a model with the Euclidean plane as canonical topology, a concrete limit on inferring one-dimensional geometry from the name tronçon.
context: S §1.2 intends non-total examples, but its ordinary product-order example needs the distinction in SP31-N009-02; E 119/32–34 supplies only a broad axiomatic program.
outcome: Verified the explicitly different strong-coordinate order using coordinatewise bounds with positive gaps; interval basis identified. See research/math_checks.md.
confidence: High: all order axioms and the interval basis are directly checked; no novelty claim.

title: The sweep’s ordinary product-order example fails a written axiom
body: S says that R² with the product order satisfies the tronçon axioms, but in the usual coordinatewise order x=(1,0) and y=(0,1) both lie strictly above a=(0,0) and have no common lower bound still strictly above a. This violates the displayed requirement that L_{>a} be downward directed. The strong-coordinate order of SP31-N009-01 is a separate valid model, not a silent reinterpretation of S’s ordinary product example.

outcome: Three-point coordinate obstruction refutes S’s example under the usual product order. Its outside-range consequence is not used as a verified counterexample here.

title: The small-cardinality shortcut includes a forbidden repeated-endpoint triple
body: The triple (a,b,c)=(0,1,0) in the ordinary rational order has a flag {a,b,c} of cardinal2, but b is neither weakly nor strictly between the equal endpoints a=c. Thus the NB’s small-cardinality alternative is too broad if treated as an equivalence defining weak betweenness. The repaired degeneracy condition requires b=a or b=c together with comparability of the remaining endpoints, with the all-equal case included; the strict-relation reconstruction can then be examined separately.

title: Recovery and intrinsic realization are different problems
locus: orientation choice and four-condition test; compare017
body: A useful next test is to separate recovery of an order from data known to come from one, from existence of an order realizing arbitrary proposed relations and pair partitions. The seed orientation and the four-point test suggest checking compatibility as the seed pair changes, but the manuscript does not prove that such local checks suffice. This could organize the open axiomatization request on017 without promoting the special recovery theorem into a general realization theorem.

The explicit proof in research/math_checks.md MC16 uses density only to recover comparability from strict betweenness; if comparability is supplied separately as on015, even density is unnecessary for this stage. The local strict-cone axioms do not enter this recovery, which sharpens the hypothesis accounting without answering the intrinsic realization question.

title: Density is essential for the disjoint-class middle test
body: On a three-element total order, each pair complement consists of the third point, so the three selected classes are distinct singletons and all three pairwise intersections are empty. Every permutation of the three-element order gives the same comparable-pair graph and pair partitions, so those data cannot distinguish the middle without an additional hypothesis. This model deliberately lacks divisibility and therefore tests the need for that hypothesis; it is not offered as a tronçon counterexample.

title: The largest category exists under the nonempty-directed convention
body: “Il y a … plus grande … T” has a direct verification when directed posets are required to be nonempty. The intended tronçon class satisfies the conditions and is stable under nonempty strict cones; conversely the categorical conditions force global directions, divisibility and the two local cone directions. The replacement of non vide by cardinal ≠1 therefore needs the usual nonemptiness convention, rather than an unqualified claim that cardinal ≠1 by itself means cardinal ≥2.
context: S§1.3/SA21-R3-04; E119/32–34 concerns proposed categories with axioms but does not establish this particular class.

title: The interval intersection statement can be proved using marked endpoints
body: The assertion that two compatible wide closed sub-tronçons intersect in another such piece, or in the empty set, follows by taking the larger lower bound and smaller upper bound among their chain-ordered endpoints. The new marked endpoints are among the old ones, proving the finite-frontier inclusion under the consistent relative-endpoint convention stated in SP31-N018-04. This order proof does not need the proposed “argument topologique,” whose identification of marked endpoints with topological boundaries fails in general.
context: S§1.4/SA21-R3-05; E119/35 warns that a boundary need not have its familiar manifold meaning; compare current023–025.
outcome: Checked intervals, rays, absent bounds and singleton/empty outcomes; research/math_checks.md MC10. Only the marked-bound convention is used.

title: Marked endpoint data are not the canonical topological boundary
body: In the valid strong-coordinate model of SP31-N009-01, [a,b] for a=(0,0), b=(1,1) is the open unit square together with its two opposite corners. Its marked endpoint set has two points, but its closure is the closed square and its topological boundary is the full perimeter; even in an ordinary bounded chain the ambient extremities require a relative-boundary convention. Thus the blanket identification on018 cannot justify the finite-frontier claims, and the later retreat on023–025 is mathematically substantive.
context: E119/35 and58 distinguishes geometric boundary data from an unjustified identification; S§1.5 notices nonclosed segments but does not supply this model.
outcome: Computed the interval, its Euclidean closure/interior and marked endpoints in an admissible tronçon. Relative-boundary convention explicitly distinguished.
confidence: High: the two sets are computed directly in the verified model; an illustrative check, not a novelty claim.

title: The boundary variable on the upper ray remains literal

title: The topological connected-component interpretation is false over Q
locus: Th 1°, bracket “les comp. conn. de U”
body: The literal bracket identifies the pieces Tᵢ with connected components, yet in L=Q the single order interval [0,1]∩Q is separated by every irrational cut between two of its points and has singleton topological components. This verifies the need for S’s correction of the interpretation, without changing the bracket or its residual U in the transcription. S’s later quotation from030 is context only; completeness has not been formalized here for all partial orders, so no blanket positive converse is asserted.

title: Uniqueness and boundary union need a combinatorial formulation
body: The page states uniqueness of the finite disjoint interval decomposition, the union formula for its finite boundary, and the implication X⊂Y ⇒ relative moderation. Divisibility proves uniqueness: a convex piece crossing two separated components would contain a point in their endpoint gap, outside the union. The full proof in research/join_check.md establishes this combinatorial uniqueness without topological connectedness, and the boundary and compatibility consequences use the consistent endpoint convention of SP31-N018-04.
context: S§1.4 carries the decomposition argument; E119/28–30 additionally retains attachment information, which this uniqueness statement does not provide.

title: The join and finite-family corollary are a distinct proof obligation
body: The margin proposes a “double récurrence” on component counts for the moderate supremum and its frontier inclusion, but does not write the induction. A full order proof is given in research/join_check.md: sort the common chain of endpoints, merge overlapping pieces into their order hulls, and use divisibility to prove that every convex input piece lies in one component of any admissible upper bound. This establishes leastness even against upper bounds whose endpoints are not compatible with the inputs; global directedness handles ray hulls. The finite-family corollary and preservation of compatibility with a third Z then follow from the marked-boundary inclusion, under SP31-N018-04’s explicit normalization.
context: S§1.4 states the calculus; E119/32–34 gives the wider motivation for stability operations on moderate parts.

title: His warning excludes a general closure operator on arbitrary subsets
body: “Il n’y a pas en général d’adh. modérée fermée” is witnessed by A={0,1/2,1/3,…} in [0,1]. Every finite union of closed intervals and points containing A contains some [0,d], and removing a small open gap between two successive reciprocals gives a smaller admissible upper set still containing A. Hence there is no least such upper set even though A is topologically closed, so the moderate operations cannot be extended to an arbitrary-subset closure operator without enlarging the family.
context: S§1.4/SA21-R3-07 already checks this warning; E119/32–34 motivates closure properties but supplies no contrary arbitrary-set claim.
outcome: Rechecked the finite-component/pigeonhole argument and the removable-gap construction; research/math_checks.md MC13.

title: Moderate join can strictly enlarge ordinary union
body: In the strong-coordinate model take a=(0,0), b=(1,1), c=(2,2): the point (1/2,3/2) belongs to [a,c] but to neither [a,b] nor [b,c]. Divisibility and compatible endpoint ordering force every admissible finite closed upper set of the two intervals to put them in the same component, so [a,c] is their moderate join. This supplies a valid non-total test of the manuscript’s distinction, independently of the sweep’s inadmissible ordinary-product example.
context: S§1.4; compare SP31-N009-01/02 and E119/34 on testing axioms in concrete models.
outcome: Verified the explicit point and interval hull in the admissible strong-coordinate order; research/math_checks.md MC11.

title: The ray-union test is exactly total comparability
body: The condition that every b be comparable with every element is exactly total order, so L_{≤b}∪L_{≥b}=L for every b expresses the stated criterion. The moderate union in the underbrace must therefore be distinguished from that ordinary union in the non-total case. This does not imply the converse from closed points to total order later queried on023; the topology sees different information.
context: S§1.4–1.5; E119/33 cautions by comparison that a structure and its topology-level comparison are different tasks.
outcome: Checked the ordinary-ray-union equivalence directly from the definition of comparability; no separation converse inferred.

In the total-order test X=[0,1], Y=[1/3,2/3], it gives Z=[0,1/3]∪[2/3,1], which meets Y in its endpoints and is not literal subtraction. This verifies the intended phenomenon in one model, but SP31-N021-04 refutes the unrestricted minimum in a valid non-total model, so the general statement cannot be carried as proved.

title: The unrestricted least moderate difference fails in the doubled line
body: In the doubled rational line let c=(−1,0), a=(0,0), a′=(0,1), b=(1,0), b′=(1,1), d=(2,0), and set X=[c,d], Y=[a,b]. The moderate complement C consists of the X-points at heights below0 or above1; both Z₀=[c,a]∪[b,d] and Z₁=[c,a′]∪[b′,d] are closed moderate supersets, but Z₀∩Z₁=C is not a finite union of closed order intervals. A least upper set would have to equal C, so the displayed unrestricted minimum does not exist; Z₁ is incompatible with Y, suggesting the distinct refinement of minimizing only among upper sets compatible with Y, which has not been proved in general here.
context: S§1.4 states the minimum without this distinction; S§1.5 supplies the doubled-line example for separation, and E119/34 motivates testing provisional axioms rather than accepting the extension.
outcome: Verified both upper sets, their exact intersection, and the impossibility of a finite closed-interval decomposition cofinal below height0 without a height0 endpoint; research/join_check.md.
confidence: High for the explicit counterexample: root and context worker checked the set calculations independently; the restricted repair remains an unproved proposal.

In the total-order test of SP31-N021-03, F={1/3,2/3} verifies the identity and is not isolated in Z; in the strong-coordinate model with X=L and Y=[a,b], the actual canonical topological frontier is an entire square perimeter. This is not the original tronçon order being identified with an Alexandrov specialization order; it is a separate containment relation on the represented lieux. The local pages give no full construction of that ficelle representation, so this assertion is carried as a manuscript claim and is not used to prove the universal statements about abstract tronçons.

title: Cone profiles compute specialization and separation directly
locus: topology generated by intervals and strict rays
body: Write D(x)={z:z<x} and U(x)={z:x<z}; for the stated canonical topology, b∈closure{a} exactly when D(b)⊆D(a) and U(b)⊆U(a). Indeed these inclusions say that every generating strict ray containing b also contains a, and the property survives intersections and unions. Consequently T₀ is injectivity of the pair (D(x),U(x)), while T₁ requires that no two distinct pairs be ordered by simultaneous inclusion, giving a direct test that does not assume an Alexandrov topology.
context: S§1.5 asks about separation; E has no matching cone-profile formula; compare RESULTS_STATE’s finite-poset variance statements only as a contrast.
outcome: Checked the generating-open characterization of closure, then T₀ and T₁; research/math_checks.md MC05.

S leaves a sobriety task open, but its viable refinement is whether every T₀ tronçon is sober; that refined question remains unresolved here. The distinction is uniqueness of a generic point, not merely existence.

title: Closed points or Hausdorff topology do not force total order
kind: self-flagged: a step he himself marks as unverified
locus: “Ce n’est que lorsque … tot ordonné” and “réciproque ?”
body: The strong-coordinate order on R² is non-total but its canonical topology is exactly Euclidean, hence Hausdorff with closed points. It therefore gives a negative answer to the converse queried here and to a necessary-condition reading of “Ce n’est que lorsque,” while preserving the sufficient total-order statement. The same model is sober because a nonempty irreducible closed subset of a Hausdorff space cannot contain two distinct points.

outcome: Verified the open-rectangle basis and disjoint-neighborhood argument for Hausdorff sobriety; research/math_checks.md MC02/04.

title: An explicit valid tronçon realizes the drawn obstruction’s inequalities
body: In the strong-coordinate model choose x=(0,−1), a=(0,0), b=(1,1), y=(2,2): a∉[x,y] while every point of ]a,b[ lies in [x,y]. In the supremum topology described in the prose, the complement of [x,y] is therefore an open neighborhood of a disjoint from ]a,b[, so a is not in its closure. This verifies the stated obstruction in a valid order model without claiming that the model is the particular topological ficelle drawn in the margin.
